invariants.rationale: A null check on the input list is frequently required for robustness and can be meaningful at method entry.
Every non-null order, if present, should have a quantity greater than zero, matching the intended validation.
Every non-null order should have a non-negative unit price, reflecting the validation logic.
No element in the list should be null, as checked during validation.
If the list is not empty, it should contain at least one non-null order, ensuring there is something to validate.
